basis: Congenital shortening of the bones of both feet's toes.
Congenital anterior urethral fold causes urinary outflow obstruction; associated infections are separate complications.
Skin, oral epithelial and corneal/lens disease define HMD; pulmonary fibrosis occurs in 30-79%. Bladder abnormalities (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia with developmental impairment and seizures; optic atrophy reported in 1/4 (25%), below the involvement threshold.
Malignant germ cell tumour arising in the ovary, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Prostate epithelial malignancy; androgen resistance does not establish an endocrine disorder. No specific metastatic organ is required by this concept.
Bacterial infection with variable anatomical sites; no single organ site is established across the umbrella concept.
Yersinia pestis infection of lymph nodes; lymphatic infection alone does not establish blood-cell or marrow disease.
Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; elevated lactate alone does not establish a separate metabolic disorder.
RELB-associated immunodeficiency with impaired T-cell function; recurrent infections are separate diseases, with no documented chronic organ damage.
Thymic epithelial tumour; thymus has no anatomical axis here. Thymoma itself is neither lymphoma nor an immune-mediated disease; immune syndromes are separate.
Malignant B-cell lymphoma; extranodal organ damage is not common enough across the group to add another axis.
Distal joint contractures and shortened Achilles tendons define the disorder.
Short telomere syndrome commonly causes marrow failure. Pulmonary fibrosis and mucocutaneous disease vary by subtype; their frequency across this umbrella is uncertain.
Glucokinase-related monogenic diabetes, usually mild stable hyperglycaemia; no additional organ damage is intrinsic to MODY2.
Infectious prion disease causing fatal nervous-system degeneration in sheep and goats; this is not a human disease.
Neoplasm occupying a cerebral ventricle, whether primary or secondary.
Inherited platelet granule and fibrinolytic bleeding disorder; joint bleeding is not established as common chronic joint damage.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease; osteoporosis belongs to a subset, with no evidence it affects at least 30% across this umbrella.
Perinatal aspiration directly injures airways and lung parenchyma; persistent pulmonary hypertension is a minority complication.
Tarsus denotes the eyelid tarsal plate; eyelid hypoplasia and absent lower eyelashes define this ocular adnexal syndrome.
Primary mesenchymal soft-tissue tumour, usually in the extremities; distant metastases are rare.
Inherited peripheral neuropathy; denervation causes distal muscle wasting and weakness in 20/20 patients. Cataracts and neutropenia are not established as common.
Sarcoma arising within the central nervous system; anatomical origin determines the axis.
Inherited testosterone-to-DHT conversion defect; perineal hypospadias is a direct urethral malformation in 80-99%. Other genital anomalies fall outside the axes.
